decisions.reason: As a close-to-core organic ham line that fits the firm's stated expansion of organic products, it would likely be kept because even with limited visible follow-up evidence a large firm has enough slack to continue a strategically aligned, low-risk extension.

Organic Kasseler is more niche than the firm's main deli staples, and with no clear sign of sustained market traction it would likely fall below aspiration levels and be dropped so resources can be used in stronger core or organic items.

Organic pepper salami matches the firm's premium cured-meat capabilities and organic direction, so management would likely tolerate some uncertainty and keep it as a plausible performer within the existing range.
The teriyaki aspic beef specialty looks like a one-off experimental deli-counter item, and absent evidence of continued support it would likely be judged below aspirations and discontinued.

Because the fennel-flavoured salami received a dedicated page and remains close to the firm's premium salami competence, management would likely see enough differentiation potential to keep it in the assortment.
The liver pâté with veal is an incremental premium variant in a category the firm already knows well, so a large established producer would likely keep it unless results were clearly poor.
